Since season 2022, Hardwood’s Discord community has conducted their own award voting, conferring honors on each year’s outstanding players.     To connect the game’s past to the present, the Retro All-American awards will crown the greatest players of Hardwood’s early seasons (2001-2021).  Each season, we’ll vote on a new year from the game’s past, traveling chronologically through Hardwood’s history.  **The Basics**  If you’ve participated in Discord All-American voting in the past, good news! The format is 90% the same. Eight D1 All-American nominees for each position with each positional winner advancing to National Player of the Year voting.   **What’s Different**  For each season, there will be a short summary of the conference and National Tournament results to give voters additional context as they cast their ballot.  You’ll also notice additional team performance info listed along with each nominee’s individual statistics.  If you’re like me and weren’t around for the game’s founding (or simply forgot how good a given team was decades ago), you may find this helpful.  Thanks for coming along for the ride as we go back to Hardwood’s first season: 2001

[2022-09-07 04:06] slickandjakenillinois : I think that’s the key. The temptation to go after the 4 and 5 star players is pretty great, but making a plan instead to get players good enough and cheap enough to land you in D1 in 3-5 years should be the short term goal.  Using the vast majority of your contacts on a star player only sets a team up for future failure, in my opinion.
[2022-09-07 06:04] naph7777 : Most people don't have the patience to play the long game. The sooner you do it the better though.  ECU http://onlinecollegebasketball.org/roster/409 1st class - only 1 scholarship open. Signed Landry(4 contacts) 2nd class - Oishi(30), Christensen(24), Paige(15) 3rd class - Neely(46) - Did not sign Juan Manuel Cuevas(60) 4th class - Connell(60), Powell(49), Carter(26) 5th class - Bates(71), Franklin(14) - Did not sign Edward Higdon(90)  By basically ignoring HS seniors the year I took them over and getting points on future classes I was able to get ahead on those guys and get them for cheaper than if I had been fighting other teams for them as seniors. It hasn't all worked out (Manuel Cuevas & Higdon), but even still it let me promote 2 seasons ago, be in contention (ultimately 5th) in LL5 last season and we should be contending for promotion to D1 again this season. That 2nd class is now Paige (6' 3" 157/11), Oishi (6' 5½" 162/12) and Christensen (6' 8½" 138/11). They have really put the team on a new trajectory.
[2022-09-07 06:07] naph7777 : That possibly reads like a massive brag... Hopefully someone can look past that and find it useful though. I imagine you could do something similar with most successful manager's 2nd teams.
[2022-09-07 10:37] slickandjakenillinois : Not a brag, but an example.  You are hoping to be in D1 after 6 seasons.  This is a roadmap on how to do it.  Nothing else matters besides focusing on getting to D1 first.
[2022-09-07 13:48] slickandjakenillinois : There were many times for NIU I had to cut ties with a main target of mine.  A bigger fish was on them and I would have to spend a lot of contacts just to have a chance to land them. That would then risk losing the other players I was recruiting. So I cut ties to secure the other recruits and found a player who may have been 5-10 SI lower but cost a lot less.  The cost and risk wasn’t worth the reward.  Humbling because I really wanted that one player, but the right decision for the future team.
[2022-09-07 13:48] naph7777 : I'm getting better at this, but its still hard once you're at High.
[2022-09-07 13:54] slickandjakenillinois : Understood.  It was never easy to make that decision.  Sometimes feels like I am a quitter, or took a hit on my pride.    But generally I would get out when on low or medium.  It did make it a little easier not having as much invested.  I never get to high on a player unless I have the contacts to defend them from being overtaken.  Inevitably it seems every season I have a player on very high and someone goes from low to high forcing me to put a few more points into them.  This year I have two of them.  But both were at very high coming into the season, so I should be way ahead of them.  But concerning anyway.

[2022-09-07 23:40] furysk : on the recruiting of seniors  -I think it's fine in specific situations.  For example, you might find a team high on a player with a scholarship offered with nobody else in on the guy, and said team has 0/X scholarships remaining.  you might be able to win a better player than the normal stuff left  -It shouldn't be used if you just took a team over and you have 9 scholarships open and you want to try to fill them all.  It hurts your ability to improve with better talent, and you are going to hit a window where you have to recruit 8-9 guys again in 4-5 years time.  -If you are recruiting in the current always, you are never building your board out.  If you never build your board out to the sophomore and juniors classes at minimum, other teams will be 30-40 contacts ahead of you at minimum by the time you get to the senior class, and you'll always be playing from behind on some of the better talent.
[2022-09-07 23:41] chousley4 : I was typing that out as you sent it! Balancing out your scholarships is key. Learned that one the hard way 😂
[2022-09-07 23:42] furysk : so it's not a "don't ever recruit seniors" it's a "know when to realize that you just need to give up on that last scholarship spot because the talent wont play enough minutes" situation
[2022-09-07 23:42] furysk : and by recruit seniors, i mean from 0 contacts 0 scholly offer
[2022-09-07 23:43] furysk : staying ahead on someone is a case by case basis and is more reasonable to do on specific guys
[2022-09-07 23:45] slickandjakenillinois : Fury’s Point 3 is a really good one and what I was eluding to. I might want to spend about 60 contacts, and no more than 100, on the current seniors.  Then get a start with an underclassmen you want.  I would stay away from 4 and 5 stars yet, you want players that aren’t going to attract a ton of competition.  Once you get that underclassmen to high, start targeting another and so on.  You hope by having them on high and having a small recruiting board others are smart enough to look elsewhere and not compete with you.
[2022-09-07 23:46] slickandjakenillinois : And I never really want more than 4 players in a class.
[2022-09-07 23:48] slickandjakenillinois : And if you have extra scholarships, I would also think about getting a Juco player if cheap and makes your team better now.

[2022-09-07 23:53] furysk : if you redshirt half, you get roughly 600 points across their recruiting cycle.
[2022-09-07 23:53] furysk : so spending 150 means you have 450 left.  Spending 150 twice means you have 300 left for the remaining 11 spots.
[2022-09-07 23:54] furysk : the 600 math is me splitting the 5th year to an easy number, as it falls somewhere between the 540 if no redshirts and 675 w/ redshirts on all.
[2022-09-07 23:54] chousley4 : Haven’t broken it down like that before. I like that.

[2022-09-07 23:56] furysk : if you spend 100 on 3, in order to balance out your expenditures to fit enough guys in you also need to get to 6 by 330 contacts overall.

[2024-04-21 17:48] _plokmijn : You get 2 points per round, there are 53 rounds per season. You get 2 points on round 0 but no points on round 53 (end of season). You can roll over up to 10 points to next season without penalty, and any points past 10 get halved for next season (22 points transfers over as 16 to next season as an example). You can have up to 45 points at any given time. At the season flip, you get 29 points.
[2024-04-21 17:48] _plokmijn : And by points I mean contacts

You spend too much time chatting up 5* Cindy and whiff and you might find that D3 me has already hooked up with your 3* backup plan Darlene 🙂
[2024-05-28 14:20] majortinkle : It really isn't. You're describing the mechanics of why it would take less contacts for lower star/desperate players to get interested quickly not for them making a decision when they supposedly could barely care less about your contacts

[2024-07-31 15:28] jerbeetwo : Please excuse the doubt implied with my question as I am trying to learn this game.  Isreal has grown 2 inches in three years so I ask how can you expect him to have two 3 inch growth spurts left surpassing his expected height by 2 inches?
[2024-07-31 15:42] _plokmijn : Projected height is next to meaningless in this game. Players will grow 3-4 times, usually totaling 7.5-8”. Israel has only had one growth spurt, so it is reasonable to expect at least 2-3 more that total about 6”. Could very well still grow going into his RS SO season.
[2024-07-31 15:50] jerbeetwo : Can you expect the same growth from International players or does this just pertain to US high schoolers?
[2024-07-31 15:52] cdilks : International players don't show up until the year before they enroll in college, so you don't have that information.
[2024-07-31 15:55] gards710 : what plokmijn is referring to is totaling growth from their HS FR season, and since INTL players don't show up until their HS SR year equivalent is why you can't put that same projection on them
[2024-07-31 16:02] gards710 : I'll admit that it is not intuitive - I also came into the game thinking that past growth spurts meant more growth to come and that if a player hadn't grown for a few years in HS, he was done. Instead, think of it like a spring: the more you compress on it (the more a player does NOT grow early on), the more it will release energy (the more growth you can expect)
[2024-07-31 16:03] gards710 : as in, the players who do not grow early on are the ones I usually project for 8+" growth
[2024-07-31 16:03] gards710 : there's ofc always exceptions

[2025-03-13 19:09] flushednevada : If you decide to show interest on a recruit, you want that interest to be to your advantage.  It’s always worth running some scenarios about how you think competitors might respond to the amount of interest you show on a recruit. There’s a whole bunch of other factors that play into it as well, like the time of the season, quality of recruit, etc. As you get a better feel for these things you can sort of model each situation a little better and make a more informed decision.
[2025-03-13 19:11] flushednevada : Sorry, that’s not a direct answer, but it’s how I think about it
[2025-03-13 19:12] squidwardfrommegamind : <@163438974885560321> I believe hambre means hunger, hombre is what you're looking for
[2025-03-13 19:14] tcm12 : Gotcha.  I'm just trying to figure out the cost/benefit of contacting them early, if that's supposed to help, with creating more competition.  On the other hand, I'm trying to weigh saving up to spend and get ahead more with not contacting them for longer
[2025-03-13 19:15] tcm12 : I'll only have 2 scholarship spots next year so I want them to at least be pretty solid.  I know I'm only DIII but I'd love to get at least one 4⭐
[2025-03-13 19:20] flushednevada : If you’re going after a recruit that is good enough to warrant attention from higher caliber programs, then I’d caution you against showing low interest for a long time. It would be better to bring them up to medium or high - it makes the idea of contesting less palatable, since you’re already in a strong position. The trade off of course being that, should you go too long without showing interest on the recruit then someone may beat you to the spot. You sort of learn to balance that, and if you’re like me you’ll get it wrong a few times while you figure it out
[2025-03-13 19:21] tcm12 : Alright thanks
[2025-03-13 19:33] gards710 : yeah, exactly what <@968180649246752839> is saying. No two situations are the same, so no one will have the right answer all the time. It's something you have to learn and get a feel for, and probably get wrong sometimes. You'll see some teams are more aggressive and others are more patient, and seeing where you fall in that will be important. Some teams target guys without any competition while others may see your team on a guy and use that as a tell to target that player. Others might just ignore you altogether.

[2025-12-09 19:35] gards710 : At the time of Carrasco's recruitment, he was dev'ing ~11 SI per year. That's not good, especially considering his POT. I know that conceptually it would make sense that POT and SI dev are directly correlated, but they really are not, at least in my eyes and experience. Players have their own intrinsic dev rates and that is separate from their POT. The POT describes their overall ceiling, and of course the further away a player is from their ceiling, the more theoretical room they have to grow and the more rapid their dev could be to reach that ceiling. But they have to have the dev to get there, or even close. Examples are the countless 10 and 11 pots that have better devs than players with higher POTs (this is my prime example for a slow dev 13 pot who never got there https://onlinecollegebasketball.org/player/169757)  Based on Carrasco's dev in HS, I did not think he would get to a useful SI in time, and for the presumed cost that an OOR 5* would cost, a 5'9" slow dev'er was not worth it. Like, could I predict that he would go +20 in each of his first two college years? No. So I was wrong about that. But what in his history would indicate that was coming?   And while yes, he was individually good for Butler. But at what cost? You demoted twice with him. Sure, you promoted twice as well. I guess that's something. The team was in shambles after he and you left. That's why I think it was not a wise investment, for multiple parties
[2025-12-09 19:54] fireballer34 : While its true about the demotions, it was actually part of my (flawed) plan. I basically recruited Carrasco and then decided to recruit only freshman from there on out. [2026-01-16 23:12] _plokmijn : I’ve always felt like prospects have the same probability to commit per day with some mechanism to commit by a certain round for high rated players (almost all 4/5* committed by round 40ish). Commitments seem like a normal probability distribution. Total players committing per recruiting round always starts a bit light, really picks up by mid season, and then tails off by the end. There is a bit more weight towards the back of the season since a chunk of the prospect population doesn’t have a scholarship offer until later on once teams start moving to their backup options. The mean commitment date for top recruits is ahead of lower rated recruits, probably to ensure that the teams that miss out have time find someone else
[2026-01-16 23:16] _plokmijn : In the case of “wants to commit on round…” players, I think they’re locked from committing before that round and then have a very high chance of committing each round once you reach their eval comment round. For example if there was a 80% chance per day of a guy committing with a round 35 comment then it’s a >99% chance he commits within 3 rounds including and after round 35

[2026-05-30 19:30] brrryse : ## **To Whom Mr. Bell Tolls**  The Bluejays have officially wrapped up their recruiting class with the commitment of **4-star Canadian point guard Archie Bell** out of Montreal, Canada.  Bell, ranked **#28 in North America**, chose Elmhurst over Assumption and projects as a stabilizing floor general for the next 4-5 years. While not the biggest guard, Bell is known for his elite basketball IQ, speed, playmaking ability, and reliable jump shot.  "Some kids play basketball. Archie understands basketball," said head coach **Rafael Ferguson**.  Bell joins a class that already featured two intriguing commitments:  **Hank Perry** (Mason, OH) — A 6'7" forward who will transition into a jumbo shooting guard role thanks to his shooting ability, speed, length, and perimeter skill set.  **Miles McCullough** (Newtown, CT) — A versatile 6'7.5" forward with a 7'+ wingspan who projects as a 3/stretch-4 at Elmhurst. McCullough brings shooting, rebounding, defensive versatility, and positional flexibility.  Taken together, the class gives Elmhurst exactly what Ferguson was seeking: size, shooting, length, versatility, and basketball intelligence.  "This class gives us options," Ferguson said. "It gives us size. It gives us skill. It gives us intelligence."  When asked whether Bell's commitment represented a turning point for the program, Ferguson smirked.  "A turning point? No. It's a beginning."  A pause.  "Besides... to whom Mr. Bell tolls?"  The room grew quiet.  "It tolls for everybody else in this conference."
